item.title: Electroencephalography as a biomarker of brain function in domestic ruminants: a systematic review and critical appraisal
item.description: BACKGROUND: Electroencephalography (EEG) has been extensively used to investigate cortical activity in ruminants under physiological, pathological, and experimental conditions. Its applications range from the assessment of consciousness and nociception to experimental models of hypoxia-ischemia, neurodevelopment, pain, anesthesia, and neurological disorders.

item.title: Immediate large-scale cortical network changes following acupuncture in patients with disorders of consciousness: a resting-state fNIRS study
item.description: Introduction Disorders of consciousness (DOC) involve severe disruption of large-scale brain networks. This study investigated immediate cortical network changes following acupuncture in patients with DOC using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).

item.title: Emergent flow theory: autonomic coherence as a gain parameter for the temporal architecture of conscious integration
item.description: Contemporary neuroscientific theories of consciousness—including Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNW), Integrated Information Theory (IIT), and the Predictive Processing/Free Energy Principle (PP/FEP)—have not formalized autonomic and neuromodulatory state as explicit dynamic control parameters within models of conscious integration. This gap constitutes the explanatory niche addressed by the Emergent Flow Theory (EFT).

item.title: Hitting and missing on consciousness
item.description: Disturbances of conscious experience are central features of many psychiatric and mental health disorders. Experimental studies of conscious perception are therefore increasingly cited in clinical and translational work under the assumption that they identify neural mechanisms specific to subjective experience.

item.title: Multimodal biomarkers of response to transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in disorders of consciousness: a study protocol
item.description: Patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC) have limited options for arousal-promoting interventions. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS), a non-invasive neuromodulation technique, has shown potential to improve conscious behaviors in a subset of patients with DOC.

item.title: Topological integration and segregation of the conscious connectome as biomarkers for state, behavior, and prognosis
item.description: Consciousness is hypothesized to emerge from a sophisticated balance between functional integration and segregation across large-scale brain networks. However, how these topological properties are disrupted in disorders of consciousness (DoC), and whether they can predict long-term recovery, remain to be established.

item.title: Assessing consciousness by near-nerve electrostimulation in intensive rehabilitation
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Consciousness diagnosis in prolonged disorders of consciousness (pDoC) relies on the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R), yet consciousness or its potential for recovery may escape behavioural detection. We tested whether Near-Nerve Stimulation (NNS) of the median nerve, compared to standard Surface Cutaneous Stimulation (SCS), could provide an EEG-based marker of consciousness and its recovery, by specifically eliciting sensory responses.

item.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Cybersecurity: A Taxonomy and Future Directions
item.description: ABSTRACT Context The rapid increase in cyber threats, coupled with increasingly sophisticated attack strategies and the exponential growth of data in recent years, has exposed significant limitations in classical machine learning, rule‐based, and signature‐based defense mechanisms. These approaches are often unable to scale or adapt effectively to evolving threat landscapes.
